newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise with hot weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise with hot weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices turned stronger Monday as temperatures in the Northeast and Gulf Coast regions neared 100 degrees F, sources said.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices were quoted about two to three cents higher at $2.16-2.18 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub.
Similarly in south Texas prices gained three cents to about $2.10.
In the Permian Basin market, prices rose six cents to about $2.08-2.09, while Waha values jumped a similar amount to $2.12-2.13.
San Juan prices were up about five cents to $2.05-2.06 as the restart of the 550 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired plant in Wyoming was delayed until Wednesday.
The 750 MW Navajo 1 coal unit in Arizona restarted as scheduled, while the 750 MW unit 5 at the Four Corners coal plant in New Mexico was still off line for nearly three weeks of repairs.
The 1,080 MW San Onofre 2 nuclear unit in California was in hot shutdown mode and preparing to restart, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC).
Southern California border prices, as a result, rose only about three cents to the low-to-mid $2.20s.
The adjacent unit 3, with a generating capacity of 1,080 MW, is slated to restart Thursday, according to the NRC.
In the Midwest, swing prices gained three cents to about $2.05-2.06. Chicago city-gate prices were quoted equally firmer at $2.22-2.24 amid highs near 90 degrees F.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate also rose several cents to the mid-$2.40s.

Helping to provide power to the sweltering region was the restart of Niagara Mohawk's 610 MW Nine Mile Point 1 and the 1,106 MW Salem 2 (operated by Public Service Enterprise Group Inc) nuclear units.
